avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Iron supplements (>325 mg elemental iron daily)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Excessive iron supplementation may cause iron overload and increase thrombotic risk when combined with ESAs
avoid_supplements.action: Monitor serum ferritin and iron levels; use only physiologic iron replacement doses

avoid_supplements.name: Androgenic steroids (DHEA, testosterone)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potentiates erythropoietic effect and significantly increases thrombotic and cardiovascular event risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; discuss alternative therapies with prescriber

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin B12 supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: B12 is a cofactor for erythropoiesis; deficiency reduces darbepoetin efficacy
caution_supplements.action: Ensure adequate B12 status; supplement if deficient (typically 1000-2000 mcg monthly)

caution_supplements.name: Folic acid supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Folic acid is required for erythrocyte maturation; deficiency impairs darbepoetin response
caution_supplements.action: Maintain adequate folate status; supplement 1 mg daily if deficient

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Enhances iron absorption and bioavailability, supporting adequate iron stores for erythropoiesis
caution_supplements.action: Monitor iron indices; vitamin C supplementation (100-200 mg daily) may be beneficial if iron-deficient

avoid_foods.name: Excessive high-iron foods without monitoring
avoid_foods.mechanism: Chronic excessive iron intake increases ferritin levels and thrombotic risk in ESA-treated patients
avoid_foods.action: Monitor serum ferritin quarterly; counsel on iron-rich food moderation if ferritin elevated (>500 ng/mL)

caution_foods.name: Iron-rich foods (red meat, fortified cereals, legumes)
caution_foods.mechanism: Dietary iron sources support adequate iron stores needed for optimal darbepoetin efficacy
caution_foods.action: Maintain balanced iron intake; monitor ferritin levels to guide dietary counseling

caution_foods.name: Folate-rich foods (leafy greens, legumes, fortified grains)
caution_foods.mechanism: Dietary folate supports erythrocyte maturation and darbepoetin response
caution_foods.action: Encourage adequate intake; ensure minimum 400 mcg daily from food sources

monitoring_notes: Monitor hemoglobin/hematocrit, serum ferritin, iron saturation, and reticulocyte count every 2-4 weeks initially, then monthly once stable. Assess for thromboembolic symptoms and maintain target hemoglobin 10-12 g/dL to minimize cardiovascular risk.
